about.label: About the project
about.manifesto: We are used to thinking that up there is emptiness. A blank page. But the emptiness has taken on density: it is filled with our presence, our ambitions, our cold metal.
about.statsHint: Press (i) on a card for the source and the date. On the debris mass you can click the number for a comparison that gives a sense of scale.
about.p1: Waste on the ground and waste in orbit are one and the same substance. A single industrial trace, which we first tore out of the planet's depths and then flung above our own heads.
about.p2: Space took the best for itself: clean metal went into rocket skins and satellite electronics. Down below there remained mountains of slag that we have learned to ignore. I am giving this matter back its right to be art. The method is called artcycling: burnt-out circuit boards, vacuum tubes and toggle switches of a great era are cleared of the layers of time and reassembled into new meanings.
about.p3: The mountains of debris in orbit are a challenge to our intellect and our spirit. We are already full and responsible residents of the Universe. It is time to behave accordingly.

history.label: Project history
history.intro: “Space Ecology” grew out of the meeting of two artistic views on the technological trace of humankind.

items.text: The monumental artist Elizaveta Kozyr created a conceptual series of works that laid the visual foundation of the theme.
Sergey Kozhukhovsky, working at the Russian Environmental Operator, made the first objects out of electronic components and gave the project its official name.
“Space Ecology” came out into public space. In the autumn the project was shown at the Renova Lab innovation centre.

A key exhibition in Kaluga, at the Tsiolkovsky State Museum of the History of Cosmonautics. As part of “Ecosophy”, the show travelled to Arkhangelsk, Tyumen, St Petersburg, Nizhny Novgorod, Yekaterinburg and Chelyabinsk.
Turning industrial archaeology into the art of the future, the project goes on widening its meanings where ecology meets space exploration.
